sources.author: Swyx (swyx)
sources.headline: Developer Relations @ Latent Space | AI Engineer
sources.post_summary: Claude's new extended thinking models are making multi-step agentic tasks dramatically more reliable. We ran 50 benchmarks comparing structured reasoning vs. vanilla prompting on tool-calling chains — the gap is now 34%. The era of 'dumb orchestration' wrappers is over.

sources.author: Luc Perkins
sources.headline: Developer Advocate @ Cloudflare Workers AI
sources.post_summary: We just shipped MCP support natively in Cloudflare Workers. You can now run a Model Context Protocol server at the edge with zero infra setup — deploy in 30 seconds. This changes how teams wire AI agents to internal tools without standing up their own backend.

sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: The biggest mistake teams make with agentic systems: they treat the LLM as the bottleneck when the real failure point is context management. Most agents fail not because the model is wrong — they fail because the model got the wrong information at the wrong time. We're releasing a new memory layer this week that addresses this directly.

sources.author: Abi Noda
sources.headline: CEO @ DX (Developer Experience) | Former GitHub
sources.post_summary: New data from 400 engineering teams: 61% have adopted AI coding assistants but only 22% report a measurable productivity gain. The delta comes down to one variable — whether the team invested in prompt hygiene and context setup upfront. Tooling is table stakes. Habits are the moat.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | GTM Advisor | Revenue Intelligence Evangelist
sources.post_summary: Most outbound teams are measuring the wrong thing. They're optimizing for reply rate when they should be optimizing for pipeline quality. I ran the numbers on 10,000 sequences last quarter — the campaigns with 3x lower reply rates generated 2x more closed-won. Here's the counterintuitive framework we used to reorient the entire motion.

sources.author: Sangram Vajre
sources.headline: Co-Founder at GTM Partners | Bestselling Author | Category Creator
sources.post_summary: GTM engineering is becoming the most important hire in B2B SaaS and most CEOs still don't know what it is. It's not sales ops, it's not marketing ops — it sits at the intersection of both and uses code + AI to compress the time between signal and action. The companies that figure this out in 2026 will have a structural advantage that compounds for years.

sources.author: Devin Reed
sources.headline: Head of Content Strategy at Clari | Ex-Gong | Helping B2B marketers drive revenue with content
sources.post_summary: Content strategy in 2026 isn't about posting more — it's about owning a signal loop. The best GTM teams I've studied treat every piece of content as a data collection instrument: what does engagement tell you about who's in-market, what pain resonates, and where the deal is in the funnel. Most teams still think of content as brand. The ones winning treat it as pipeline intelligence.

sources.author: Jen Spencer
sources.headline: CEO at SmartBug Media | RevOps Advocate | Helping revenue teams scale without chaos
sources.post_summary: RevOps teams are drowning in tech debt and nobody's talking about it. We audited 40 mid-market stacks this year — the average company is paying for 14 tools that overlap on core functions, and 6 of those tools have zero adoption past the first 90 days. Before you automate your outbound, you need to fix your data model. Bad data + AI = faster garbage at scale.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Indie hacker | Shipped 3 products in 90 days | ex-Google PM
sources.post_summary: Priya shares that she quit her PM job at Google 6 months ago with $40k saved and just crossed $8k MRR. She breaks down the exact stack she used (Next.js, Stripe, Resend), how she found her first 10 paying customers on Reddit, and what she'd do differently. Ends with her real P&L screenshot.

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Solo dev → SaaS founder | Vibe coding my way to ramen profitability
sources.post_summary: Marcus posts a raw, unfiltered look at shipping his 7th micro-SaaS in 18 months — 6 of which made $0. He describes the exact moment his current tool clicked, how he used Claude Code to cut build time from 3 weeks to 4 days, and why he stopped listening to 'validate before you build' advice. 847 words of no-BS honesty.

sources.author: Daniela Romero
sources.headline: Nurse turned software engineer | 18 months, 0 CS degree, hired at a startup
sources.post_summary: Daniela documents the exact curriculum she followed to go from ICU nurse to a hired frontend engineer — no bootcamp, just free resources, personal projects, and 400+ rejected applications. She lists the 3 portfolio projects that actually got callbacks, the salary she negotiated, and what nursing taught her about debugging under pressure.

sources.author: James Okafor
sources.headline: Building AI tools for small businesses | Shipping every week | $0 → $3k MRR
sources.post_summary: James posts his weekly ship log: what he built, what broke, what users actually said. This week: he added a Slack integration his users begged for, it took 6 hours, and it immediately became the top reason people upgraded to paid. He includes a Loom link showing the feature and the Stripe notification that followed.
